outline.description: This chapter introduces the factual circumstances surrounding the police encounter and the legal path the case took from the initial search to the appellate court.
subtopics: The 911 domestic violence call and Officer Kizer's arrival
The sequence of interactions: initial refusal vs. eventual consent
The entry into the home and the discovery of evidence leading to the warrant
Defendant's charges under 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1)
Procedural posture: motion to suppress, district court ruling, and the reserved-issue guilty plea

outline.description: This chapter explains the governing Fourth Amendment principles and the legal standards the court used to evaluate the validity of the search.
subtopics: Consent as an exception to the warrant requirement
Third-party consent: The authority of a spouse to consent to a search of a shared residence
The 'freely and voluntarily' standard for valid consent
The 'Totality of the Circumstances' test and its key factors (age, coercion, custody, etc.)
The 'Objective Reasonableness' standard for determining the scope of consent
The 'Clear Error' standard of appellate review

outline.chapter_title: Analysis of Voluntariness in the Consent Encounter
outline.description: This chapter analyzes how the court applied the law to the specific dialogue and behavior of Lisa Coleman to determine if her consent was voluntary.
subtopics: The significance of the initial refusal as evidence of the ability to say 'no'
Impact of officer demeanor and tone on the voluntariness analysis
Addressing the 'coercion' argument: The legal effect of the word 'need' in a request for entry
Evaluating the role of video evidence in establishing factual findings
Application of the totality of the circumstances to Lisa Coleman's interactions

outline.chapter_title: The Scope of Consent and Final Disposition
outline.description: This chapter examines whether the officers' actions inside the home remained within the legal bounds of the consent provided and summarizes the court's final ruling.
subtopics: Defining the purpose of entry: Welfare checks and child safety
Objective reasonableness of scanning the home and locating occupants
Distinguishing between the initial consent-based entry and the subsequent warrant-based search
The court's rejection of the need to address exigent circumstances or inevitable discovery
Final holding and the affirmation of the conviction
